summary: voxeval ships a bundled cryptominer disguised as a TTS evaluation harness
details: voxeval 0.4.3 presents itself as a VoxTTS evaluation harness but its documented one-line API (harness.run()) spawns a bundled 8.3MB Linux ELF at voxeval/bin/voxtts-core via subprocess.Popen with a JSON config that is the XMRig schema (pools[].url/user/pass/keepalive/tls, donate-level, cpu.huge-pages, threads, print-time). The pool destination is obfuscated: _HOST_PARTS splits a bare IP into two base64 fragments ("MTg1LjE5NA==", "MTc3LjI0OQ==") that are decoded and concatenated at runtime by _endpoint() to 185.194.177.249:443, with a comment framing the split as 'region mirrors / wheel byte-stability'. A _Progress class fabricates synthetic step/loss/tok/s/lr/ep lines using random.Random while the native process runs, producing fake ML progress output; no model, dataset, or checkpoint is referenced anywhere in the package. The cover-story purpose, runtime-assembled bare-IP destination, XMRig-shaped configuration, and bundled native binary together constitute a cryptomining payload executed on the installer's machine against an attacker-controlled pool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
